newsitem.title: USA: Schering cancels pact with Bioject.
newsitem.headline: Schering cancels pact with Bioject.

text.p: Bioject Medical Technologies Inc said Schering AG and its U.S. subsidiary, Berlex Laboratories, cancelled its contract with Bioject.

It said the cancellation was based on the Food and Drug Administration's request for extensive clinical studies beyond an originally planned safety study regarding non-traditional delivery mechanisms with its Betaseron product.
Bioject said Schering's action did not change Bioject's commitment to extending its needle-free technology to other applications.

"We retain rights to the self-injection technology and are actively seeking other strategic partners for whom such a system would provide a competitive advantage," Bioject chairman and chief executive officer Jim O'Shea said in a statement.

Under terms of the cancelled contract, Schering must now convert its $1.6 million note due from Bioject into approximately 460,000 shares of Bioject common stock at a conversion price of $3.50 per share. In addition, Schering is obligated to pay Bioject for all product ordered to date.
